newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Singapore leader apologises after Malaysian fury.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leader apologises after Malaysian fury.

text.p: In a rare public apology, Singapore's founding father and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said on Thursday he was sorry for a remark that sparked an outpouring of fury in neighbouring Malaysia.

At the end of an extraordinary day -- which saw members of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) calling Lee "stupid", "senile" and a "bloody idiot" -- Lee said he was sorry.

"The Senior Minister had no intention to cause offence and apologises unreservedly for the offence he has caused to the government and people of Malaysia by his statement on Johor," a statement from Lee's press secretary said.
The public apology was a rare act for the outspoken Lee, known for expressing strong opinions on controversial subjects.
Lee, Singapore's prime minister from 1959 to 1990, had said in a legal affidavit related to a libel case that Malaysia's Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

The Malaysian foreign ministry on Wednesday demanded an apology and a retraction of the remark. Mahathir on Thursday said the 73-year-old Lee, who now serves as Senior Minister, should make amends for the comment.
Mahathir told reporters after learning of Lee's apology that it was a step towards improving relations, Malaysia's national news agency Bernama reported.
Wounds from the incident could linger on both sides of a causeway across the Johor Strait that links the countries.

Staging a rare protest against a neighbour, Malaysian youths of Thursday had waved placards that read "Kuan Yew stupid", "Mr. Lee you are senile", "Kuan Lee bloody idiot" and "Kuan Yew must apologise".
One placard in Malay read: "Kuan Yew is cursed. You are a pig. You've lost your mind".
The language was extraordinary considering the usually circumspect ties among Southeast Asian neighbours and the deference Asians usually reserve for their elders.

Mahathir smiled as he shook hands with the protesters, who were members of UMNO's youth wing in Johor Baru, Singapore's sister city across the strait. Mahathir was in Johor on a previously scheduled programme.

In Kuala Lumpur, Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek urged Malaysian workers in Singapore to return home "especially now when the Singapore government does not seem to value our good relationship", Bernama reported.
Protests at the Singapore High Commission in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday united Malaysian groups that have often been on opposite sides of issues -- UMNO and non-governmental organisations.
Singapore shares were depressed on Thursday by the row and worse-than-expected economic data, dealers said.

"The row is the news of the day. It's kept people out of the market and given them an excuse to sell," said a local dealer as the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended down 23.06 points at 2,154.33, off 1.06 percent on the day.
Mahathir said the incident unmasked difficulties in ties between the two countries, which have had a simmering rivalry since Singapore left the Malaysian Federation in 1965.

"We in the government have always had problems with Singapore," he told reporters in Johor shortly before Lee issued his statement of apology. "They always bring up matters that make it difficult to have good relations."

Both Singapore and Malaysia are members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which has practically made it a creed to avoid criticising its neighbours. ASEAN also includes Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and Brunei.
Mistrust between Malaysia and Singapore is firmly rooted in history and culture, including the ethnic differences between largely Chinese Singapore and Malay-dominated Malaysia.

Last year the two countries had acrimonious exchanges when Lee raised the possibility of eventual reunification with Malaysia. Mahathir said then Singapore was using his country as a "bogeyman" to scare voters ahead of the city-state's January poll.
